Internal Readiness Prompt: Risks to impartiality are identified, reviewed and controlled.
Customer and laboratory information is protected and disclosure controls are defined.
Laboratory responsibilities, authority and organizational interfaces are defined.
Competence, qualification, authorisation and ongoing monitoring are controlled.
Facilities and environmental conditions are suitable, monitored and recorded where relevant.
Equipment is suitable, identified, maintained, calibrated where required and protected from invalid use.
Measurement traceability is established and supported by appropriate calibration/reference evidence.
External suppliers affecting laboratory results are evaluated and controlled.
Test demand is reviewed for method, capability, capacity, acceptance criteria and customer needs before commitment.
Methods are controlled by revision and non-standard/laboratory-developed methods are validated before routine use.
Where sampling is performed, plans, methods, records and sample identity are defined and controlled.
DUT/sample identity, condition, storage, handling and disposition are controlled.
Technical records preserve sufficient information to reconstruct test execution and evidence.
Measurement uncertainty is evaluated where relevant to validity or decision rules.
Quality-control activities are used to monitor and demonstrate validity of results.
Reports are complete, traceable, reviewed and clearly identify results and relevant conditions.
Complaints are received, evaluated, investigated, tracked and resolved with appropriate independence.
Nonconforming laboratory work is controlled, impact assessed and dispositioned.
Laboratory information systems and calculations are protected, validated and controlled.
Policies, objectives and management-system information needed for consistent laboratory operation are defined and maintained.
Management-system documents are approved, current at point of use and protected from unintended use of obsolete information.
Records are identified, retained, protected, retrievable and dispositioned in a controlled manner.
Risks and opportunities affecting laboratory objectives are identified and acted upon.
Improvement opportunities and customer/laboratory feedback are evaluated and used to improve the management system.
Root cause, action, effectiveness and recurrence prevention are demonstrated for nonconformities.
Internal audits cover the management system and laboratory activities on a planned basis.
Management review uses performance, risk, resources, complaints, audit and improvement inputs.
